There’s some thought provoking themes about perception of self, self growth, and fame. Mina’s transition from pop star to actress is extremely messy. It’s hard to tell how much of it is her own desire to grow versus pressure from her agency. The transition spurs an internal struggle for Mina to reconcile the image of the pop idol that she left that everybody wants to trap her in and the person that she’s trying to become. It’s a well written story, but in execution, it started to feel a bit repetitive and several scenes felt unnecessary/uncomfortable to watch. Would not recommend this broadly and probably won’t rewatch, but wasn’t a waste of time.

You could say I’ve found myself in a Double Bind. I’m incredibly torn on this. The film is both undoubtedly ahead of its time and deeply of its time. It has a complete and total understanding of fandom and stan culture most contemporary films should be jealous of, before either had even been born let alone matured to what they are now. The psychological examination of Mima is fascinating and the film abandons all tradition when it comes to structure to force its audience into her perspective and feel as though you’re losing your mind along with her. However, in the twisty third act that level of intense scrutiny when it comes to Mima’s psychology is left by the wayside. I’m not a fan of the Rumi twist. When a film is entirely about the inner workings of someone’s mind and then suddenly decides to be about someone else’s sudden mental break I’m just left a little annoyed. It’s not even that it feels like it comes out of nowhere but that it’s so much less interesting. Suddenly the film is about a bitter, older, fatter woman desperately deluding herself as she cloys for the attention a younger, prettier, thinner girl is getting. A played out trope that’s usage here borders on misogynistic? Mima’s struggle isn’t about perfection (which is why the claim Black Swan ripped this movie off beat for best makes no sense to me, clearly took inspiration but the cores are so different) it’s about identity. So the personification of her struggle with identity no longer being a part of her but someone else seems to undermine that journey. Especially, because once Rumi is revealed, the film ends and Mima is perfectly fine and self assured again. I just feel underwhelmed. Something so interesting becomes so dull. It feels like the film is dedicated to trying to tell an earnest story about being a woman in the spotlight and in some places it succeeds but in others it feels like it falls directly in line with what it’s trying to critique. I’m not someone that thinks rape or sexual assault should never be depicted. Artists have a right to create art about anything they want to. These things are real so of course there should be stories about them. And while the sexual assault and rape scenes (whether real ir acted) are intentionally disturbing in an affective way, they also seem to be drawn and directed in such a way to titillate the viewer. Now, I understand that this is a film about voyeurism and it’s absolutely drenched in metaphor. I don’t think this is just some misogynistic torture porn it’s not that simple. I think it tries to be a story exposing the horrific reality many women face, whether that be the threat of sexual violence or being pressured and pushed into uncomfortable situations or society’s crazymaking obsession with youth and fame and attention being forced upon them. I think in some places it succeeds and in some places it fails. Part of me thinks a big reason why this has the reputation it does is because it’s an anime and if this same film were made in live action there would be less fondness for it. And I mean it is a very well animated film although not much differentiates it from most anime I’ve seen on a technical level. On a thematic level I think everything here is pushing towards a cohesive whole. Every element has something to do with fame and audience and compromise and voyeurism and obsession. There is a thematic throughline here that is definite. But that seems to come at the expense of a throughline for our narrative and characters. Which I’m often more than happy to look past but here so much of this film is built around character. It’s almost a character study of Mima for most of its runtime. So to have that element become so muddled is a real shame. I did really enjoy my time with this. It’s so disorienting and thrilling but I struggle to look past how disappointed I was with the ending, and it’s half baked condemnation of misogyny and rape culture.

I’m not sure about this to be honest, the whole rape fantasy sequences is really what puts me off to be honest and it’s very off putting and very unnecessary?? However, The whole exploration of Mima’s identity is incredibly well structured with her not being able to tell what is real and what is not, a real psychological warfare throughout the whole runtime. quite a trippy and confusing film but it was good and different from a lot of films I've seen. it's a film that discusses explicitly how much control the patriarchy has over women, and esp how women in the entertainment industry barely have any control over themselves and what they want to do, that doesn't matter to the industry, everything mira "agrees" to hurts her, mentally and physically, she is used and sexualised and only agrees to it bc she feels she has to, "this is just a part of the business" and she doesn't really realise that she can say no, not that it would matter if she did. this lack of care ntrol she has spirals throughout the film as she has no idea whats going on anymore, what she's done and can't distinguish dreams from reality, emphasising how little control she has over her own life, so much that it's barely even hers anymore and she just tunes in at random moments. and the ending shows how men's "ownership" of women in the industry has always been happening, rumi represents what mira could have become, and rumis persona being pop idol mira clearly shows how much being a pop idol herself with all the expectations affected rumi, while she was not successful like mira was she still clung onto her past bc it is likely when she felt the most desired in an industry and world where approval (esp from men) is key to success, (and who doesn't want to be loved/adored?) so she separated herself as she is from who she used to be/wanted to be as a way of coping (and I think that she also experienced sexual assault like mira did, which definitely impacted her, I think esp bc of her reaction to mira doing the tape scene). however, since it did have a few scenes of sexual assault (one in an acting setting but still) and personally I don't like seeing those in media I don't think I will be watching this film again but it does a very deep dive into the horror of the exploitation of women in the entertainment industry.

The work is amazing rather it’s my feeling towards it that leaves me with a 3 star. While the concepts are very much realistic but they made me uncomfortable due to the extreme nature and disturbing perception that this movie portrays. Maybe if it we’re to consider it as insight into mental health and social issues it helps translate these concepts, however in the context of a general message from a movie it rather drained me and damaged my spirit abit. Sooooo… if it’s ur cup of tea ur in for a great movie if not then sorry for that.
